entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: This application is filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking anticipatory bail.

2. The petitioners are the 1 st and 3rd accused in Crime No.157 of 2023 of Kumbla police station,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 448, 427 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The prosecution allegation is that on 02.03.2023 at about 11.55 p.m., the accused persons, with the intent to cause wrongful loss to ULCCS (Uralungal Labour Contract Cooperative Society) caused damage to the weighbridge by inserting a circuit chip.

It is alleged that when the materials for the construction of the NH project at Thalappady-Chengala NH Road were weighed, the weight of the steel was shown to be more than its actual weight, and the company sustained a loss of Rs.50 lakhs.
Thus, the accused have committed the aforesaid offences.
4. I have considered the rival contentions.
5. It is seen that this Court had granted an interim order, on 11.08.2023, which is extracted below:
"After considering all the relevant aspects, I deem it appropriate to pass an interim order in this case.
Accordingly, it is ordered that the petitioners shall surrender before the investigating officer within a period of two weeks from today to subject themselves to interrogation.

After such interrogation, in the event of arrest, the petitioners shall be released on bail upon they execute a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.

This order shall be in force for a period of four weeks."
6.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that pursuant to the above order, the petitioners who are accused 1 and 3 had surrendered before the Investigating Officer as directed and have been enlarged on bail.

7. In such circumstances, I am inclined to pass an order making the earlier interim order absolute,
subject to the following conditions:
ii) The petitioners shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer and shall appear as and when directed by the Investigating Officer.

ii) The petitioners shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses, tamper with any evidence or get involved in similar offences while on bail.
iii) The petitioners shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional court.
